title: Shader Forge: Procedural Material Workshop
description: The user operates a shader forge where interlocking gears drive a procedural material pipeline. By adjusting shader parameters through UI sliders and clicking interactive hotspots, the user crafts a custom material that is live-previewed on a ShaderBall, while an animated box serves as a secondary preview target showing the material under deformation.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive shader forge workshop. Load three GLB assets using GLTFLoader: gears.glb (centered at origin, scale to fit ~2 units), ShaderBall2.glb (positioned at x=3), and BoxAnimated.glb (positioned at x=-3, play its AnimationMixer clip in a loop). Set up a PerspectiveCamera at (0,3,10) looking at origin, with OrbitControls. Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and two directional lights from opposing angles (intensity 1.0 each). Create a custom ShaderMaterial with uniforms: u_time (float), u_noiseScale (float, range 1-20, default 5), u_colorA (vec3, default red), u_colorB (vec3, default blue), u_distortion (float, range 0-2, default 0.5), u_metallic (float, range 0-1, default 0.3), and u_pulseSpeed (float, range 0.1-5, default 1.0). The vertex shader should displace vertices along normals using a sine-based distortion controlled by u_distortion and u_time. The fragment shader should mix u_colorA and u_colorB using a 3D simplex-style noise pattern scaled by u_noiseScale, modulated by a pulsing factor driven by u_pulseSpeed and u_time, with a fake metallic reflection term using view-direction dot normal powered by u_metallic. Apply this ShaderMaterial to all meshes in ShaderBall2 and BoxAnimated by traversing their scenes. The gears model should rotate continuously around Y-axis; its rotation speed must be linked to u_pulseSpeed so faster pulse means faster gears. Build an HTML overlay panel with 6 labeled range sliders controlling: noiseScale, distortion, metallic, pulseSpeed, and two color pickers for colorA and colorB. Each slider change updates the corresponding uniform immediately. Add a 'Randomize' button that sets all parameters to random valid values with a smooth 0.5s tween. Add a 'Screenshot' button using renderer.domElement.toDataURL. Validate that all 6 parameters stay within their defined ranges. The animation loop updates u_time and the AnimationMixer each frame.
